title: New Orleans clarinet, trombone and saxophone styles; Eddie Miller
summary: Kelly says clarinet and trumpet were New Orleans' distinctive instruments and calls Eddie Miller an original stylist.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: And always of the instruments that I think the new audience playing, I think the clarinetist and of course trumpet, trombone, except for good tailgate and good playing, well, of course, Charlie Miller and Julian Lane played well and there were others. But there never was a tromboneist example like Jack or, of course, there weren't many of those ever. But today, of course, the style that he created is used by everybody to some extent. But just somehow, to me, except for Brunus and Santo and the others, who played well, beautiful. But they were not, they didn't create any particular style, Dick, I don't think. Well, tailgate was something that they perfected to some extent. They, they, the blacks have done it always. But, the clarinet and trumpet are distinctive instruments. I don't think saxophone even, but the way the saxophone players were at all comparable to the, to the clarinetists. They just always had wonderful clarinet players and the black players, you know, like Bonnie and so many others, who were one of my favorites of all time.
And, if you had to name a single famous New Orleans saxophone player, you could name one, I'd say. Eddie Miller, of course.

Eddie, Eddie is an original. Yeah. In a sense, he, he certainly created a style of his own. His playing is distinctive. He's an extremely talented man. And probably, if you wanted to hear his clarinet playing, I don't know, Leon Rapolo's playing real well. But, it's my feeling probably that Eddie would probably play more like him than anybody. If you listen to some of the quirky courses that he made that would have even credited to him, they would amaze you. Have you heard the Bud Brown record with Eddie? Oh, yeah.
I got that. I guess Bud gave it to me on, either him or the guitar player. I mean, you know.
Eddie, Eddie does play some clarinet on there.

Not the guitar player. The guy who wrote one of the pieces on there. He's a guitarist. Yeah. Eddie, of course, he disclaims being in shape on clarinet. And I heard him record with Johnny Armand on clarinet. Oh, he? He said he hadn't played it for nine years or something like that.
